description: Per-rule metadata (why it matters + source citation) attached to Finding objects produced by app/ats_engine/rules_structure.py and rules_sections.py. IMPORTANT: none of these are backed by a live-fetched citation yet -- confidence is honestly set to E (internal heuristic) across the board. Phase 9 (app/research/) is where real WebFetch-sourced citations with an actual URL and date-accessed get attached, replacing these placeholders one rule at a time. Do not upgrade a rule's confidence level without a real source recorded here.

multi_column.why_it_matters: Multi-column layouts are commonly cited as an ATS risk because some parsers read left-to-right across the full page width rather than down one column before the next, interleaving unrelated content (e.g. a date from the right column landing mid-sentence in the left column's job description).

tables.why_it_matters: Tabular layouts are commonly cited as inconsistently parsed by older ATS configurations -- cell contents can be dropped, merged, or read out of the intended row/column order.

text_boxes.why_it_matters: Text placed in a floating text box/shape sits outside the normal document text flow. Many parsers extract only the main flow, so text-box content can be invisible to the ATS even though it is fully visible to a human reader.

hidden_text.why_it_matters: Hidden (w:vanish) or white-on-white text is invisible to a human reviewer opening the file normally. If an ATS or a recruiter later opens the raw text, this reads as an attempt to game keyword matching, which is a credibility/integrity risk independent of whether it helps parsing.

header_footer_contact.why_it_matters: Contact information placed only in a document header or footer is commonly cited as being skipped by some ATS text-extraction configurations, which read the main body content and may ignore header/footer regions entirely.

image_only_page.why_it_matters: A page with no extractable text layer (a scanned image or a flattened/rasterized page) cannot be read by any text-based ATS parser at all -- this is the highest-confidence structural risk this engine can flag, and it is directly observed (no text layer found) rather than inferred.

extraction_disagreement.why_it_matters: When independent extraction methods produce substantially different text for the same document, that divergence is itself evidence of a parsing-fragile layout -- different ATS vendors use different underlying PDF/DOCX text extraction libraries, so disagreement here predicts inconsistent results across real ATS platforms.

uncommon_font.why_it_matters: Uncommon or highly stylized fonts occasionally substitute poorly or extract with broken ligatures in some PDF-to-text converters. This is a lower-confidence, extraction-hygiene flag, not a claim that the specific font was tested.

missing_section_heading.why_it_matters: Some ATS platforms bucket resume content into fields (experience, education, skills) using recognized section-heading text as the delimiter. A missing or unconventional heading for a standard section can mean that content is not correctly attributed to the right field.

missing_contact_field.why_it_matters: Most ATS platforms create the candidate record from parsed contact fields (name, email, phone). A field the parser cannot find at all cannot populate that field in the ATS record, independent of layout quality elsewhere.
